ai.description: This small turtle reaches 13 cm. It has a dark brown, flattened carapace with a serrated rear margin and a yellow-streaked head. Its plastron is distinctively hinged and lacks a bridge.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Cochin Forest Cane Turtle is best identified by its unique, deeply serrated posterior shell margin and a distinct, dark-bordered yellow stripe along its head.
ai.habitat: The Cochin Forest Cane Turtle inhabits evergreen forests and moist deciduous woodlands within the Western Ghats, typically at elevations between 400 and 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Cochin Forest Cane Turtle is primarily crepuscular and exhibits a unique defensive strategy by tightly retracting its head and limbs into its shell when threatened.
ai.reproductionNotes: The Cochin Forest Cane Turtle is oviparous, laying a small clutch of 1–2 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically between June and September.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Cochin Forest Cane Turtle is endemic to the Western Ghats of Kerala and Karnataka, typically inhabiting evergreen forests at elevations between 300 and 1,000 meters.
